Some steps of this book were also checked in Lean, a proof assistant. They
live in a separate Lean package, the Lean companion. Its public release 0.9.0,
\begin{center}\small
\href{https://github.com/chenle02/stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/tree/v0.9.0}{\nolinkurl{github.com/chenle02/stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/tree/v0.9.0}}\\
DOI~\href{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24199105}{10.5281/zenodo.24199105},
\end{center}
contains the state described here: its Lean sources and configuration are
identical to commit 6eb79c7 of the development repository, its own receipts
bind its root commit, and its file \texttt{provenance/DEVELOPMENT.md} maps it
to the development commits cited here.
This appendix lists, for each numbered result of the book that the companion
covers, how much of it Lean checks.

The Lean work is still in progress, and the list will become more complete
with time. This appendix records what had been checked by machine at one
fixed version of the companion: commit \lcCommit{}, made on \lcDate{} at
\lcTime{}. All the checks reported below were run on that version, and the
list is generated from its coverage file. A later version may cover more.

Three points apply to every row. First, Lean checks the statements as they
are written in Lean. Second, whether those statements say what the book says
was reviewed by AI models of a different family from the ledger's author; it
has not been checked by a person. Third, the analytic and probabilistic
inputs stay outside Lean: the solution of the stochastic wave equation, the
Stratonovich integrals and the noise, the bounds imported from the
literature, the passage from Laplace transforms to time, and the variational
asymptotics. Where a row says that inputs are supplied, they enter Lean as
named hypotheses.

The statements added in wave L9, and the changes that wave made to existing
entries of the coverage record, were checked against the book in eight
independent correspondence reviews, done by AI models from a different family
than the one that wrote the formal statements. The reviews found documentation
corrections only, and no error in a Lean proof. The corrections were made and
re-checked over ten confirmation rounds. During them the author fixed three
conventions for the record: a result counts as formalized in full only if every
conclusion is a Lean conclusion under the book's hypotheses, and otherwise the
missing part is named; a result about an object the companion models by a
registered standard choice counts in full, while a result that needs an object
the companion does not construct counts as narrower; and the record's index
lists, for each label, only the sections where it is treated. A final
confirmation passed with high confidence, and the author accepted wave L9 on
November~12, 2026, with a correction of the count of public definitions
recorded as a documentation-only successor. The record states what remains
open. The exact occupation-ceiling constant is now formalized, but
Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling} stays narrower, because its second
sentence is not formalized and the class of occupation fields is modelled by
joint representatives. The Fock form is proved with a bound on its
spatial column supplied as an input.
The Green-kernel part of
Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms} holds in dimensions one to three, but
the lemma stays narrower because the smoothing of the covariance is not yet
identified. Lemma~\ref{L:finite-word-cutoff} is formalized for one Gaussian
mode per color only. These reviews are not a human verification, and they do
not check the analytic inputs that stay outside Lean.

The companion was built and checked with lean-pkg~\cite{chen:26:lean-pkg},
a tool for registering and checking Lean packages that the author developed
(version~\lcLeanPkgVersion). For commit \lcCommit, lean-pkg records that the
package builds from scratch with no unproved steps, and that every public
declaration, and each of the \lcClaimsChecked{} listed claims, uses only
Lean's three standard axioms (\texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and
\texttt{Quot.sound}). A second, separate check confirms that the proofs of
all \lcComparatorTheorems{} theorems prove their statements as restated in a
separate file. The list of claims has \lcVerified{} verified and \lcOpen{}
open. These checks concern the Lean statements themselves; whether those
statements say what the book says is the AI-reviewed match described above.
Every module of the Lean library was also checked a second time by Lean's
separate kernel checker, run on a computing cluster; three helper libraries used
only for the separate statement check were not.
\fi
